subject: Marketplace retainer & ramp framework for annual prepay (Azure/GCP)
body:
----Message 1 (2026-11-02 09:12 - Tim Hart <tim.hart@cloudscale.com>)
From: Tim Hart <tim.hart@cloudscale.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, procurement@cloudscale.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring annual prepay + ramp credits for Azure private offer

Soojin / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — product looked strong. Our procurement and cloud teams are asking whether we can structure an annual prepay via the Azure private offer that builds in a small ramp for the first 6 months and an upfront onboarding credit to cover migration costs. High level asks: 1) 12-month prepay with quarterly true-ups, 2) a ramp schedule where 40% of committed consumption is available year 1 and the remainder phases in, 3) an onboarding credit against the first invoice, and 4) a marketplace offset to account for Azure fees.

Can you share a working framework (discount tiers, credit schedule, billing cadence) we can review internally?

Tim
VP, Platform Engineering
CloudScale Inc

----Message 2 (2026-11-02 10:06 - Soojin Lee reply)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Hart <tim.hart@cloudscale.com>, Angela Ruiz <angela.ruiz@microsoft.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring annual prepay + ramp credits for Azure private offer

Tim — great to hear from you. Appreciate the detail; attached is a first-pass framework tailored to an Azure private offer and a companion commitment matrix (attachment). Key points up front: 

- Term: 12-month annual prepay (upfront charge) with quarterly consumption true-ups.
- Ramp: Year 1 availability set at 40% of contracted annual units across months 1–6, then linear ramp to 100% by month 12. True-ups reconcile usage above ramp in quarterly cycles.
- Discounting: 8% baseline term discount at $Xk ARR-equivalent; 12% discount if commit >= 1.5x baseline; addl 2% for 3-year prepay.
- Onboarding credit: One-time credit equal to 5% of first-year committed value applied to invoice 1.
- Marketplace offset: We propose a 1.5% marketplace fee credit to offset Azure marketplace commissions (applied as a billing credit).
- Billing cadence: Upfront invoice, quarterly true-ups, and a modest monthly usage report delivery.

I've attached: commitment_matrix.xlsx (breakdown of discount bands and monthly ramp), RI_private_offer_form_azure.docx (filled with proposed lines). Please review and we can iterate.

Sincerely,
So-jin Lee
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: commitment_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 78KB)]
[attachment: RI_private_offer_form_azure.docx (document, 42KB)]

----Message 3 (2026-11-02 11:33 - Rishi Malhotra internal)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace retainer framework for CloudScale (numbers)

Sojin — reviewed the matrix. A few internal asks before we finalize: 

1) Discount floors: 8% baseline is acceptable but finance prefers using a stepped credit approach rather than compounding discounts — keep the headline discount but move the additional 2% (three-year uplift) into an annual price guarantee for year 2/3.
2) Onboarding credit: 5% is fine but we need to tie it to deliverables (migration milestone 1) and cap at $75k.
3) Marketplace offset: rather than a flat 1.5% credit, propose linking offset to net invoice as a line item so auditors can track marketplace fees separately.
4) Billing: propose quarterly invoices (upfront + qtr true-ups) to simplify CloudScale accounting.

I'll model incremental ARR impact if we adjust ramp to 50% availability in Y1 vs 40%. Marcus, any floating-rate concerns on the marketplace form?

-Rishi
Director, Revenue Operations
[internal attachment: projected_revenue_impact.xlsx (12KB)]

----Message 4 (2026-11-02 13:04 - Marcus Lin internal)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace retainer framework for CloudScale (numbers)

Rishi — linking the marketplace offset as a discrete line item is correct for auditability. Also flagging: Marketplace private offers sometimes require revenue recognition adjustments on our side depending on how the offset is applied. Ops suggests we use a "credit reserve" account and amortize onboarding credits over 6 months to match delivery.

On ramp: 50% Y1 availability will help CloudScale get to product-market fit faster, but it increases short-term capacity pressure. If CloudScale wants 50% availability in Y1, we should either: a) increase upfront payment 10% to guarantee capacity, or b) keep payment flat but include a burst buffer (metered) with explicit overage rates.

-Marcus
Head of Retail Revenue

----Message 5 (2026-11-03 08:27 - Soojin reply to external with internal notes)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Hart <tim.hart@cloudscale.com>, Angela Ruiz <angela.ruiz@microsoft.com>, procurement@cloudscale.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace retainer & ramp framework for annual prepay (Azure/GCP)

Tim / Angela — thanks for the request and for looping procurement. Per internal review we've updated the framework attached (commitment_matrix.xlsx v2):

- Baseline discount: 8% (applied to committed units).
- 3-year option: price protection in years 2–3 rather than an additional up-front % discount; we will hold year-2 list rates flat for the committed SKU bundle.
- Onboarding credit: 5% of first-year committed value capped at $75k, paid as a billing credit and amortized over the first 6 months (internal accounting).
- Ramp alternatives: 40% availability year 1 (default) OR 50% availability if CloudScale agrees to either a 10% higher upfront payment or a burst buffer at published overage rates.
- Marketplace offset: line-item credit (1.5% suggested) shown separately on the invoice for auditability.
- Billing cadence: Upfront invoice + quarterly true-ups; we can switch to quarterly invoices if procurement prefers less reconciliation.

Please see attached PO draft for procurement to review. Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the matrix.

Best,
So-jin Lee
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: commitment_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 82KB)]
[attachment: CloudScale_PO_Draft_v3.pdf (pdf, 210KB)]

----Message 6 (2026-11-04 09:41 - Tim Hart external follow-up)
From: Tim Hart <tim.hart@cloudscale.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, angela.ruiz@microsoft.com, procurement@cloudscale.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace retainer & ramp framework for annual prepay (Azure/GCP)

Sojin — thanks, that layout helps. A couple clarifying questions from procurement and finance: 

1) If we select the 50% Y1 availability with the 10% higher upfront payment, how will refunds/true-ups work if actual consumption is below ramp in Q1/Q2?
2) For the onboarding credit cap ($75k), can we convert any unused portion into a professional services credit for migration support rather than a straight refund?

Would like to get our legal/procurement folks on a call Thurs; we can do 10:00am PT or 4:00pm PT.

Regards,
Tim

----Message 7 (2026-11-05 17:45 - Soojin final reply scheduling call)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Hart <tim.hart@cloudscale.com>, procurement@cloudscale.com
Cc: angela.ruiz@microsoft.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace retainer & ramp framework for annual prepay (Azure/GCP)

Tim — thank you. Quick answers before the call: 

1) Refunds/true-ups with 50% availability + 10% higher upfront: any unused commitment will be reconciled at the quarterly true-up rate. If consumption falls below committed ramp, CloudScale may elect to convert shortfall into a paid professional services engagement (migration/optimization) at agreed SOW rates or request a cash refund for the true-up amount. We prefer conversion to PS credit where feasible; it helps both sides accelerate adoption.
2) Unused onboarding credit: yes, we can convert unused portion into PS credit (migration hours) up to the $75k cap — we'll include language in the private-offer form.

Call scheduled: Thu Nov 6, 2026 10:00am PT (30 minutes) — calendar invite to follow.

Looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
So-jin
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
